narrative_purpose: Shows the famous lab demo: a small disc locked in mid-air at a tilt above a magnet track, even hanging below it - proof the lock is real and hands-off.
subject: A small flat circular disc held rigidly in the air above a flat track made of square magnet tiles. The disc floats at a clear fixed gap and is frozen at a slight tilt, not falling. A wisp of cold white vapour drifts off the disc (it is very cold). Beside it, a second smaller inset shows the same track flipped upside-down with the disc hanging underneath it, still held, not falling.
scene: A clean dark laboratory surface; the magnet-tile track and the locked disc, with faint cold vapour. The small inset in a corner shows the upside-down case.
camera: Close three-quarter view of the disc and track, emphasising the fixed floating gap and the tilt.
light: Cool lab lighting, a cyan glow in the gap between disc and track, pale vapour catching the light.
palette: Dark surface, pale disc, teal magnet tiles, cyan glow in the gap, white cold vapour.
detail_level: High detail on the disc, the gap, and the vapour; the inset simpler.
composition: Main disc-and-track in the lower two-thirds; small upside-down inset in an upper corner.
consistency_notes: Gap glow is the same cyan as the chapter's flux threads, tying the lab demo to the mountains; disc clearly does not touch the track.
negative_prompt: no text, no logos, no hands, no wires, no contact between disc and track, no oversaturation
